title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The count eats and is set free; the exiles grow rich (tiradas 60–63, lines 1024–1086)
part: Tiradas 60–63 · The count eats and is set free; the exiles grow rich (lines 1024–1086)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 195–198, lines 1024–1086 (tiradas 60–63). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Mio Çid R[o]y Diaz odredes lo que dixo:
“comed co[m]de, deste pan e beved deste vino.
sentences.l:
My Çid Roy Díaz you-will-hear what he-said:
“eat, count, of-this bread and drink of-this wine.
sentences.i: Hear what my Çid Ruy Díaz said: “Eat, count, of this bread, and drink of this wine.
sentences.n: Tirada 60 (assonance í-o) — the Çid promises the count his freedom (Pidal: El Cid promete al conde la libertad). The line-ends are í-o (dixo, vino, cativo, cristianismo). R[o]y, only the o Pidal's (his italics), as elsewhere. odredes = oiréis, 'you will hear', the minstrel turning to his audience (future of oír, syncopated). co[m]de, the m Pidal's, as in the last part. deste = de este: 'of this bread', a partitive, 'some of this bread'.

sentences.t:
Si lo que digo fiziéredes, saldredes de cativo;
si non, en todos vuestros días non veredes cristianismo.”
sentences.l:
If what I-say you-do, you-will-come-out from captive;
if not, in all your days not you-will-see Christendom.”
sentences.i: If you do as I say, you will come out of captivity; if not, in all your days you will never again see Christendom.”
sentences.n: fiziéredes = hiciereis, the future subjunctive, normal in Old Spanish after si for a future condition (f- for h-, as everywhere). saldredes = saldréis, 'you will come out', future of salir with a d slipped in (salré > saldré). de cativo, 'from captivity', cativo 'captive' used for the state. cristianismo, 'Christendom', the Christian lands: the count would die a captive, never again among Christians.

sentences.t:
—“Comede, don Rodrigo, e penssedes de folgar,
que yo dexar mê morir, que non quiero comer [al].”
sentences.l:
—“Eat-you, don Rodrigo, and may-you-think to rest,
for I to-let me-will die, for not I-want to-eat other.”
sentences.i: “You eat, don Rodrigo, and take your ease; for I will let myself die, for I do not want to eat anything at all.”
sentences.n: Tirada 61 (assonance á) — the count refuses (Pidal: Negativa del Conde). The line-ends are a stressed á (folgar, al, acordar, pan), with grandes (1031) counting as á, its unstressed final e not counting. Comede, the imperative comed with a final e. penssedes de folgar: Pidal's note to v. 1028, 'descansad, estad tranquilo', 'rest, be at ease'; folgar = holgar (f- for h-), the subjunctive penssedes serving as a polite command. dexar mê morir: the split future, infinitive + pronoun + he: me dexaré morir, 'I will let myself die'. Pidal prints mê with a circumflex, the me and the he run together (as lâ at v. 914 and lês at v. 975 were). que … que, 'for … for'. [al], Pidal's restoration (in italics): al, 'anything else, other'; non … al, 'nothing else', i.e. nothing at all.

sentences.i: Up to the third day they cannot bring him round; while they are sharing out this great booty, they cannot make him eat a morsel of bread.
sentences.n: nol = non le, 'not him'. acordar: Pidal's note to v. 1030, 'No pueden persuadirle', 'ponerle en buen acuerdo', 'they cannot persuade him', 'bring him to a good mind'. ellos partiendo, 'they dividing', an absolute gerund: 'while they were dividing'. ganançias, 'gains, booty'. muesso, 'a bite, a morsel' (the word is from Latin morsum, 'bite'; Pidal gives no note).

sentences.t:
Dixo mio Çid: “comed, co[m]de, algo,
ca si non comedes, non veredes cristianos;
sentences.l:
Said my Çid: “eat, count, something,
for if not you-eat, not you-will-see Christians;
sentences.i: My Çid said: “Eat something, count, for if you do not eat, you will never see Christians again;
sentences.n: Tirada 62 (assonance á-o) — the Çid repeats his promise to the count, sets him free and sends him on his way (Pidal: El Cid reitera al conde su promesa. — Pone en libertad al conde y le despide). The line-ends are á-o (algo, cristianos, pagado, dalgo, mano, alegrando, fablado …, ending at salvo, año, penssado). 1033b is Pidal's own b-line, keeping the traditional count. algo, 'something'. ca, 'for'.

sentences.t:
e si vos comiéredes don yo sea pagado,
a vos, [el comde], e dos fijos dalgo
quitarvos e los cuerpos e darvos e de mano.”
sentences.l:
and if you eat whereof I be satisfied,
to you, the count, and two sons of-something
free-you I-will the bodies and give-you I-will of hand.”
sentences.i: and if you eat so that I am satisfied, you, the count, and two of your noblemen, I will set your persons free and let you go.”
sentences.n: don yo sea pagado: Pidal's note to v. 1034, don, 'de lo cual', 'whereof'; 'si no coméis a mi satisfacción', 'if you do not eat to my satisfaction' (the paraphrase is put negatively, as at v. 1054). pagado, 'satisfied, content' (pagar, 'to please'). [el comde], wholly Pidal's (in italics). fijos dalgo, 'sons of something', men of birth, noblemen (fijo dalgo = hidalgo): two of the count's knights taken with him. quitarvos e … darvos e: read here as two split futures, quitar vos he and dar vos he, the he 'I will' written e (as dar vos he de mano at v. 1040 spells it out); so 'I will free you … I will release you'. Read as the conjunction e, the line would leave the si of v. 1034 with no finite verb to answer it (only bare infinitives), and v. 1040 gives the same verb with he spelled out: the split futures are the reading the syntax requires, though Pidal gives no note on the spelling. Pidal's note to v. 1035b: quitar, 'libertar', 'to set free'; dar de mano, 'soltar', 'to let go'. los cuerpos, 'the bodies', i.e. your persons.

sentences.t:
Quando esto oyó el co[m]de, yas iva alegrando:
“Si lo fiziéredes, Çid, lo que avedes fablado,
tanto quanto yo biva, seré dent maravillado.”
sentences.l:
When this heard the count, already-himself he-was rejoicing:
“If it you-do, Çid, what you-have spoken,
as-much as I may-live, I-will-be thereof amazed.”
sentences.i: When the count heard this, he began to brighten: “If you do it, Çid, what you have said, for as long as I live I shall marvel at it.”
sentences.n: yas = ya se, the se cut to s: yas iva alegrando, 'he was already cheering up', ir + gerund. fiziéredes, future subjunctive after si; lo is announced, then spelled out by lo que avedes fablado, 'what you have spoken'. tanto quanto yo biva, 'as long as I live' (biva = viva, subjunctive). dent = de + ent (a form of ende), 'of it, thereof'. maravillado, 'amazed, full of wonder': the count does not expect a captor to keep such a promise.

sentences.t:
—“Pues comed, co[m]de, e quando f[ó]redes yantado,
a vos e a otros dos dar vos he de mano.
sentences.l:
—“Then eat, count, and when you-will-have dined,
to you and to others two give you I-will of hand.
sentences.i: “Then eat, count, and when you have dined, you and two others I will set free.
sentences.n: f[ó]redes = fuéredes, future subjunctive of ser, the ó Pidal's: ser as the auxiliary with yantado, 'when you have dined' (yantar, 'to dine, eat the main meal'). dar vos he de mano = vos daré de mano, the split future, 'I will let you go' (dar de mano, 'to release', as Pidal glosses at v. 1035b).

sentences.i: But of all that you have lost and I won on the field, know that I will not give you back one wretched penny: for I need it for these men who go with me in hardship.
sentences.n: quanto, 'all that'. en canpo, 'in the field', in battle. sabet = sabed, 'know'. [de ello], Pidal's restoration (in italics), 'of it'. un dinero malo, 'a bad penny': the dinero was a small coin; non … un dinero, 'not a penny'. huebos me lo he = lo he menester, 'I have need of it' (huebos, 'need', from Latin opus). lazrados, 'toiling, suffering hardship' (lazrar, 'to suffer, labour'): the exiles live hard. 1044-5 is a single line carrying two numbers; Pidal prints it so. The number 1043 is printed nowhere in his verse column: the count simply passes from 1042 to 1044-5, and the text follows his print.

sentences.i: Taking from you and from others, we shall go on paying ourselves; we shall lead this life as long as it pleases the holy Father, as one who lies under the king's anger and has been cast out of his land.”
sentences.n: ir nos hemos pagando = nos iremos pagando, the split future with ir + gerund: 'we will go on paying ourselves', taking our wages from what we seize. abremos = habremos, 'we shall have, lead'. mientra = mientras. ploguiere, future subjunctive of plazer, 'it may please'. Pidal's note to v. 1047: esta vida, 'that of the omne airado por su rey (the man under his king's anger), that is, el desterado' (so printed, for desterrado, 'the exile'; compare v. 882), 'who had to keep himself at the cost of wars and plunder. For that reason airado was often a synonym of malhechor, "evildoer", just like another equivalent word, "foraxido" (exido fuera, desterrado: "gone out, exiled"), and for that reason too the vida airada came to be taken in a bad sense.' commo que, 'as one who' (Pidal gives no note; a causal 'since' is also possible, with the same sense in the end); ira a = ira ha (a the h-less spelling of ha, as at v. 1008), 'has the anger of the king', i.e. lies under the king's ira, his formal displeasure. es echado, 'is cast out': the Çid speaks of himself in the third person, as of the type of the exile.

sentences.t:
Alegre es el conde e pidió agua a las manos,
e tiénengelo delant e diérongelo privado.
sentences.l:
Glad is the count and asked water for the hands,
and they-hold-it-to-him before and they-gave-it-to-him quickly.
sentences.i: The count is glad, and he asked for water to wash his hands; they hold it before him and gave it to him at once.
sentences.n: agua a las manos, 'water for the hands', the washing that began a meal. tiénengelo … diérongelo: gelo = se lo, 'it to him', glued to the verb; tienen, present, then dieron, preterite: the poem's tense-mixing. delant, 'before (him)'. privado, 'quickly'. conde is here written with n, without Pidal's restoration.

sentences.t:
Con los cavalleros que el Çid le avie dados
comiendo va el co[m]de ¡Dios, qué de buen grado!
sentences.l:
With the knights that the Çid to-him had given
eating goes the count — God, how of good will!
sentences.i: With the knights the Çid had given him, the count sets to eating — God, how gladly!
sentences.n: le avie dados, 'had given him', the participle dados agreeing with los cavalleros (the two knights of v. 1035). comiendo va, ir + gerund. ¡Dios, qué de buen grado!, 'God, how willingly!', the minstrel's own exclamation; de buen grado, 'gladly'.

sentences.t:
Sobrél sedie el que en buen ora nasco:
“Si bien non comedes, co[m]de, don yo sea pagado,
aquí feremos la morada, no nos partiremos amos.”
sentences.l:
Over-him sat he who in good hour was-born:
“If well not you-eat, count, whereof I be satisfied,
here we-will-make the stay, not ourselves we-will-part both.”
sentences.i: Beside him sat he who was born in a good hour: “If you do not eat well, count, to my satisfaction, we shall make our stay here; we two shall not part.”
sentences.n: Sobrél = sobre él. Pidal's note to v. 1053: 'junto a él estaba', 'he was beside him'; sobre expresses position beside a person in a higher place, or dominating him in any way (compare vv. 2285, 3689). sedie, 'was sitting' (seer). el que en buen ora nasco, the 'born in a good hour' formula. don yo sea pagado, as v. 1034. feremos la morada, 'we will make the stay' (feremos = haremos). amos = ambos, 'both': the Çid will keep the count here, and stay with him, until he eats.

sentences.t: Aquí dixo el co[m]de: “de voluntad e de grado.”
sentences.l: Then said the count: “of will and of liking.”
sentences.i: Then the count said: “Willingly, and gladly.”
sentences.n: Aquí, here 'then, at this'. de voluntad e de grado, 'willingly and gladly', the same pair as at v. 1005.

sentences.t:
Con estos dos cavalleros apriessa va yantando:
pagado es mio Çid, que lo está aguardando,
por que el co[m]de don Remont tan bien bolvie las manos.
sentences.l:
With these two knights in-haste goes dining:
satisfied is my Çid, who him is watching,
because the count don Remont so well was-turning the hands.
sentences.i: With these two knights he falls to his dinner briskly; my Çid is well pleased as he watches him, because Count Remont is plying his hands so well.
sentences.n: apriessa, 'quickly, eagerly'. va yantando, ir + gerund. pagado, 'pleased'. aguardando, 'watching, keeping an eye on'. por que, 'because'. bolvie las manos, 'was turning (moving) his hands': the count's hands busy between dish and mouth; bolvie = volvía, imperfect in -ie.

sentences.t:
“Si vos ploguiere, mio Çid, de ir somos guisados;
mandadnos dar las bestias e cavalg[a]remos privado:
del día que fue co[m]de non yanté tan de buen grado,
el sabor que de[n]d e non será olbidado.”
sentences.i: “If it please you, my Çid, we are ready to go; have the mounts given us and we will ride at once. Since the day I became count I have never dined so gladly; the relish I have of it will not be forgotten.”
sentences.n: Si vos ploguiere, 'if it please you' (future subjunctive). guisados, 'ready, prepared'. mandadnos dar, 'order (them) to give us'. bestias, 'beasts', the mounts. cavalg[a]remos, the a Pidal's. fue = fui, 'I was': Pidal's note to v. 1062, fué for 'yo fui' is still used today in certain dialects. yanté, 'I dined'. el sabor, 'the taste, the delight'. de[n]d e: dend = de ende, 'of it', the n Pidal's; e is read as he, 'I have', here the full verb aver, 'to have, hold', not the future auxiliary of vv. 1035b and 1040: 'the delight I have of it'. olbidado = olvidado.

sentences.t:
Danle[s] tres palafrés muy bien ensellados
e buenas vestiduras de pelliçones e de mantos.
El co[m]de don Remont entre los dos es entrado.
sentences.l:
They-give-them three palfreys very well saddled
and good garments of fur-robes and of mantles.
The count don Remont between the two is entered.
sentences.i: They give them three palfreys, very well saddled, and good clothing, fur robes and mantles. Count Remont has taken his place between the two.
sentences.n: Danle[s], the s Pidal's: 'they give them'. palafrés, 'palfreys', riding horses (not war-horses). ensellados, 'saddled'. pelliçones, 'fur robes' (pelliza, a fur-lined garment). es entrado, 'has entered', ser as the auxiliary of a verb of motion: he rides between his two knights.

sentences.t:
Fata cabo del albergada escurriólos el Castellano:
“Ya vos ides co[m]de, a guisa de muy franco,
en grado vos lo tengo lo que me avedes dexado.
sentences.l:
To end of-the camp escorted-them the Castilian:
“Now you go, count, in manner of very frank,
in thanks to-you it I-hold what to-me you-have left.
sentences.i: The Castilian saw them off to the edge of the camp: “Now you go, count, free as a Frank; I thank you for what you have left me.
sentences.n: Fata = hasta, 'as far as'. cabo, 'end, edge'. albergada, 'camp'. escurriólos: Pidal's note to v. 1067, 'los salió a despedir', 'he went out to see them off' (compare vv. 2590, 2640); los glued on. el Castellano, 'the Castilian', the Çid. a guisa de, 'in the manner of'. muy franco: Pidal's note to v. 1068, a play on words with the two meanings of franco, 'catalán' and 'libre, exento', 'Catalan' and 'free, exempt' (the Catalans are los francos at v. 1002); the English 'frank' can carry 'free' only faintly, so the interpretive line names both: 'free', and 'a Frank', as the Catalans are called in the battle of the last part (v. 1002). en grado vos lo tengo, 'I hold it in thanks to you', 'I am grateful'; lo is announced and spelled out by lo que me avedes dexado: the booty, said with a smile.

sentences.i: If it should come into your mind that you would like to avenge it, if you come looking for me, send me word first: either you will leave me something of yours, or carry something of mine away.”
sentences.n: emiente: Pidal's note to v. 1070, 'recuerdo, idea', 'memory, thought'; venir emiente, 'to come to mind'. vengallo = vengarlo, the r of the infinitive assimilated to the l of the pronoun. viniéredes buscar, 'you come to seek', venir + bare infinitive. fa[zedme antes] mand[ado]: Pidal restores, in italics, the letters zedme antes and the ado of mandado, 'make me beforehand a message', i.e. send me warning; fazedme = hacedme. The exact span of the italics was hard to read on the scan and is uncertain. 1072-3 is one line carrying two numbers. o … o, 'either … or'; the initial o may also be printed in italics (a restoration), which is uncertain on the scan. dexaredes, 'you will leave'; levaredes = llevaréis, 'you will carry off'. de lo vuestro … de lo mio, 'of what is yours … of what is mine'.

sentences.i: “Rest easy, my Çid, you are quite safe. I have paid you enough for this whole year; coming after you will not even be thought of.”
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1074: 'Estad tranquilo, oh Cid, bien libre estáis de eso', 'Be at ease, O Çid, you are quite free of that'. Folguedes, subjunctive as a polite command (folgar, 'to rest'). ya, the vocative 'O'. sodes = sois. en vuestro salvo, 'in your safety', safe. Pagado vos he, 'I have paid you', with a wry turn: the booty taken from him is his payment for the year. aqueste = este. venirvos buscar, 'to come to seek you'. sol non, 'not even' (sol = solo, 'only', here 'so much as'; not the noun sol, 'sun').

sentences.t:
Aguijaba el co[m]de e penssava de andar,
tornando va la cabeça e catándos atrás;
sentences.l:
Was-spurring the count and was-thinking to go,
turning goes the head and looking-himself behind;
sentences.i: The count spurred on and set off on his way, turning his head again and again and looking back;
sentences.n: Tirada 63 (assonance á) — the count leaves, mistrustful; the wealth of the exiles (Pidal: El conde se ausenta receloso. — Riqueza de los desterrados). The line-ends are a stressed á (andar, atrás, repintrá, ha, Bivar, alegrar, grand, an), with alguandre (1081) counting as á, its unstressed final e not counting. Aguijaba, 'spurred', printed with b (elsewhere aguijava). penssava de andar, 'set about going' (pensar de + infinitive). catándos = catándose, 'looking himself', catar 'to look', with se glued on.

sentences.t:
miedo iva aviendo que mio Çid se repintrá,
lo que non ferié el caboso por quanto en el mundo ha,
una deslea[l]tança ca non la fizo alguandre.
sentences.l:
fear he-was having that my Çid himself would-repent,
what not would-do the excellent-one for as-much-as in the world there-is,
a disloyalty for not it he-did ever.
sentences.i: he was afraid that my Çid would change his mind — a thing the worthy man would not do for all there is in the world: a disloyalty, for never in his life did he commit one.
sentences.n: miedo iva aviendo, 'he went having fear', ir + gerund. se repintrá = se arrepentirá, 'will repent', a syncopated future of repentirse (repentirá losing its unstressed i, the e raised to i: repintrá). ferié = haría, conditional. el caboso: Pidal's note to v. 1080, 'el Cid' (compare v. 226): caboso, 'excellent, accomplished', used as a noun. por quanto en el mundo ha, 'for all there is in the world' (ha = hay). deslea[l]tança, 'disloyalty', the second l Pidal's. ca, 'for'. alguandre, 'ever'; non … alguandre, 'never'. The line restates v. 1080 in apposition; its syntax is loose.

sentences.t:
Ido es el co[m]de, tornós el de Bivar,
juntós con sus mesnadas, conpeçós de [a]leg[r]ar
de la ganançia que han fecha maravillosa e grand;
tan ricos son los sos que non saben qué se an.
sentences.l:
Gone is the count, turned-himself he of Bivar,
joined-himself with his troops, began-himself to rejoice
for the gain that they-have made marvellous and great;
so rich are the his-men that not they-know what themselves they-have.
sentences.i: The count is gone; he of Vivar turned back, joined his companies, and began to rejoice over the gain they have made, marvellous and great: so rich are his men that they do not know what they have.
sentences.n: Ido es, 'is gone', ser as auxiliary of motion. tornós, juntós, conpeçós = tornó se, juntó se, conpeçó se, each with se glued on: 'turned back', 'joined', 'began'. el de Bivar, 'he of Vivar'. mesnadas, 'companies, household troops'. [a]leg[r]ar: the a and the first r are Pidal's restorations (in italics); conpeçós de alegrar, 'began to rejoice' (comenzar de + infinitive). fecha = hecha. los sos, 'his men'. qué se an, 'what they have', se the subject's own interest, an = han. Line 1085 is not here: Pidal prints it at the head of the next tirada, at the opening of the Cantar II, so 1086 follows 1084 directly; his numbers are kept.
